missions.title: Picnic Market
missions.topic: much · many · some · any · there is / are
missions.subtitle: Pack food for the picnic
missions.guide: Read the food clue. Tap a word block to pack the picnic basket!
missions.reminder: Count carrots: many carrots. Milk is an amount: much milk. Use some in these positive sentences and any after isn't.

tasks.prompt: How ___ apples are there? We can count apples.
tasks.full: How many apples are there?
tasks.hint: Apples can be counted. Use many.
tasks.explain: Use many with countable plural nouns such as apples.

tasks.prompt: How ___ water is in the bottle?
tasks.full: How much water is in the bottle?
tasks.hint: Water is an amount, not separate items.
tasks.explain: Use much when asking about an amount of water.

tasks.prompt: We have oranges. There are ___ oranges in the bag.
tasks.full: There are some oranges in the bag.
tasks.hint: This positive sentence says we have oranges.
tasks.explain: Some gives a positive amount without an exact number.

tasks.prompt: The glass is empty. There is not ___ milk in it.
tasks.full: There is not any milk in it.
tasks.hint: Not makes this sentence negative.
tasks.explain: Use any after not to say there is no milk.

tasks.prompt: Two bananas are on the table. There ___ two bananas.
tasks.full: There are two bananas on the table.
tasks.hint: Two bananas means more than one.
tasks.explain: There are goes with a plural noun such as bananas.

missions.title: My Things Bridge
missions.subtitle: Return the lost belongings
missions.guide: Read who owns each thing. Tap the right block to return it!
missions.reminder: Use my or her before a noun. Mine and his can show ownership without repeating the noun.

tasks.prompt: I own this bag. It is ___ bag.
tasks.full: It is my bag.
tasks.hint: The speaker says I own it.
tasks.explain: My shows that something belongs to the speaker.

tasks.prompt: A girl has a red hat. This is ___ hat.
tasks.full: This is her hat.
tasks.hint: Use her for something belonging to the girl.
tasks.explain: Her is a possessive adjective used before hat.

tasks.prompt: A boy owns this kite. The kite is ___.
tasks.full: The kite is his.
tasks.hint: A boy owns the kite. Choose his.
tasks.explain: His can stand alone to show that the kite belongs to the boy.

tasks.prompt: I own the blue book. The blue book is ___.
tasks.full: The blue book is mine.
tasks.hint: The speaker owns the book. Use mine without another noun.
tasks.explain: Mine means the book belongs to me.

tasks.prompt: The bag belongs to Ali. It is ___ bag.
tasks.full: It is Ali's bag.
tasks.hint: Add apostrophe s to Ali to show ownership.
tasks.explain: Ali's shows that the bag belongs to Ali.

missions.title: Daily Train
missions.subtitle: Spot a routine or an action now
missions.guide: Read the time clue. Put the word carriages in order to move the train!
missions.reminder: Every day tells us about a routine. Now tells us an action is happening: am, is or are + an -ing word.

tasks.prompt: Build a routine sentence. Start with I.
tasks.full: I walk to school.
tasks.hint: Start I walk. Put to school at the end.
tasks.explain: I walk describes a routine in the present simple.

tasks.prompt: Describe what she is doing now. Start with She.
tasks.full: She is reading now.
tasks.hint: Use She is, then reading, then now.
tasks.explain: She is reading describes an action happening now.

tasks.prompt: Describe the boys now. Start with They.
tasks.full: They are eating lunch.
tasks.hint: Use They are before eating.
tasks.explain: Use are with They in the present continuous.

tasks.prompt: Describe a daily routine. Start with We; finish with every day.
tasks.full: We drink water every day.
tasks.hint: Put We drink water before every day.
tasks.explain: Every day shows a routine, so use drink with We.

tasks.prompt: Describe Ali on Sundays. Start with Ali; finish with on Sundays.
tasks.full: Ali plays football on Sundays.
tasks.hint: Use Ali plays football, then on Sundays.
tasks.explain: A singular subject such as Ali takes plays for a present simple routine.

missions.title: Wish River
missions.topic: like / enjoy / love + ing · want + to
missions.subtitle: Tell us what you enjoy or want
missions.guide: Put the word blocks in order. Build a wish or a favourite activity!
missions.reminder: Enjoy goes with an -ing word: enjoy playing. Want goes with to + a verb: want to play. Love can also go with an -ing word.

tasks.prompt: Say what you like. Start with I.
tasks.full: I like reading books.
tasks.hint: Put reading after like.
tasks.explain: Like can be followed by an ing form such as reading.

tasks.prompt: Say what you want. Start with We.
tasks.full: We want to swim.
tasks.hint: Put to before swim.
tasks.explain: Use want to followed by the base form swim.

tasks.prompt: Say what she enjoys. Start with She.
tasks.full: She enjoys playing games.
tasks.hint: Put playing after enjoys.
tasks.explain: Enjoys is followed by an ing form, so use playing.

tasks.prompt: Say what they love. Start with They.
tasks.full: They love drawing cats.
tasks.hint: Use drawing after love.
tasks.explain: Love can be followed by an ing form such as drawing.

tasks.prompt: Say what he wants. Start with He.
tasks.full: He wants to eat.
tasks.hint: Use He wants, then to eat.
tasks.explain: Use wants with He, followed by to and the base verb eat.

missions.title: Memory Mine
missions.topic: Past actions · helped · went · saw · could
missions.subtitle: Find memories and past skills
missions.guide: Read the past clue. Mine the word block that completes the memory!
missions.reminder: Yesterday and last night are in the past. Help becomes helped, go becomes went, and see becomes saw. Could describes a past ability.

tasks.prompt: Yesterday, I ___ Mum in the kitchen.
tasks.full: Yesterday, I helped Mum in the kitchen.
tasks.hint: Yesterday tells us the action is in the past.
tasks.explain: Helped is the past form of help.

tasks.prompt: Last night, we ___ a film.
tasks.full: Last night, we watched a film.
tasks.hint: Use the past form ending in ed.
tasks.explain: Watched is the regular past form of watch.

tasks.prompt: Yesterday, they ___ their grandmother.
tasks.full: Yesterday, they visited their grandmother.
tasks.hint: Add ed to visit for this past action.
tasks.explain: Visited is the past form of visit.

tasks.prompt: We go to the park on Sundays. Yesterday, we ___ to the zoo.
tasks.full: Yesterday, we went to the zoo.
tasks.hint: Go changes to went in the past.
tasks.explain: Went is the irregular past form of go.

tasks.prompt: I can swim now. When I was five, I ___ swim too.
tasks.full: When I was five, I could swim too.
tasks.hint: When I was five refers to ability in the past.
tasks.explain: Could is the past form of can and shows past ability.

missions.title: Tomorrow Portal
missions.topic: am / is / are going to · future plans
missions.subtitle: Make a plan for tomorrow
missions.guide: Read each plan. Tap the correct block to open tomorrow's portal!
missions.reminder: For a plan, use am, is or are + going to + a verb. I am going to plant. She is going to plant. We are going to plant.

tasks.prompt: Tomorrow, I ___ going to draw a cat.
tasks.full: Tomorrow, I am going to draw a cat.
tasks.hint: Use am with I.
tasks.explain: I am going to describes a future plan.

tasks.prompt: Tomorrow, she ___ going to visit her aunt.
tasks.full: Tomorrow, she is going to visit her aunt.
tasks.hint: Use is with she.
tasks.explain: She is going to describes her future plan.

tasks.prompt: We have a plan for Saturday. We ___ going to play football.
tasks.full: We are going to play football.
tasks.hint: Use are with we.
tasks.explain: Use We are going to for a shared future plan.

tasks.prompt: Ali has a ticket for tomorrow. He is going ___ travel by bus.
tasks.full: He is going to travel by bus.
tasks.hint: The pattern is going to plus a base verb.
tasks.explain: Use going to travel, not going at travel.

tasks.prompt: They have a picnic plan. They are going to ___ sandwiches.
tasks.full: They are going to make sandwiches.
tasks.hint: After going to, use the base form of the verb.
tasks.explain: Make is the base verb used after going to.

missions.title: Reason Rescue
missions.subtitle: Explain how to help the cat
missions.guide: Read the cat's clue. Choose a reason to help the rescue team!
missions.reminder: Why asks for a reason. Because introduces a reason: We help the cat because it is cold.

tasks.prompt: I drink water ___ I am thirsty.
tasks.full: I drink water because I am thirsty.
tasks.hint: Being thirsty is the reason for drinking water.
tasks.explain: Because links the action to its reason.

tasks.prompt: She wears a coat ___ it is cold.
tasks.full: She wears a coat because it is cold.
tasks.hint: The cold weather is the reason.
tasks.explain: Use because to give the reason for wearing a coat.

tasks.prompt: Why are you eating? I am eating ___ I am hungry.
tasks.full: I am eating because I am hungry.
tasks.hint: A Why question asks for a reason.
tasks.explain: Because I am hungry answers the Why question.

tasks.prompt: It is raining. Why is Ali using an umbrella?
tasks.full: Ali is using an umbrella because it is raining.
tasks.hint: Choose the reason that matches the rain.
tasks.explain: The rain explains why Ali is using an umbrella.

tasks.prompt: Mia wants to read. The room is dark. Why does she turn on the light?
options: Because she needs to see the book.
tasks.answer: Because she needs to see the book.
tasks.full: Mia turns on the light because she needs to see the book.
tasks.hint: A light helps Mia see in a dark room.
tasks.explain: The reason connects the dark room with reading the book.

missions.title: Tower Castle
missions.topic: taller than · shorter than · bigger than · smaller than
missions.subtitle: Compare the castle objects
missions.guide: Look at the labels and sizes. Tap the object that matches the comparison!
missions.reminder: Taller and shorter compare heights. Bigger and smaller compare sizes. Than tells us which other object to compare with.

tasks.prompt: Tap the taller tower.
tasks.full: Tower B is taller than Tower A.
tasks.hint: Look for the tower that reaches higher.
tasks.explain: Tower B reaches higher, so it is taller.

tasks.prompt: Tap the shorter tower.
tasks.full: Tower B is shorter than Tower A.
tasks.hint: The shorter tower does not reach as high.
tasks.explain: Tower B is lower than Tower A, so it is shorter.

tasks.prompt: Tower A is on the left. Tap the tower that is taller than Tower A.
tasks.full: Tower B is taller than Tower A.
tasks.hint: Compare the two heights. Tower B reaches higher.
tasks.explain: Taller than compares the heights of two towers.

tasks.prompt: Tower B is on the right. Tap the tower that is shorter than Tower B.
tasks.full: Tower A is shorter than Tower B.
tasks.hint: Look for a tower lower than Tower B.
tasks.explain: Tower A is shorter because it does not reach as high as Tower B.

tasks.prompt: Look at both towers. Tap the bigger tower.
tasks.full: Tower A is bigger than Tower B.
tasks.hint: The bigger tower is shown at a larger size.
tasks.explain: Bigger than compares the sizes of the two towers.

rules: shop
Food and amounts
many apples · much water · some oranges · not any milk
Use many for countable things and much for an amount. Use some in these positive sentences and any after not.
How many apples are there? There is not any milk.
bridge
Whose things?
my bag · her hat · the kite is his · the book is mine
My and her come before nouns. Mine and his can stand alone. Add apostrophe s to a name to show ownership.
It is Ali's bag. The blue book is mine.
train
Routines and now
I walk · Ali plays · she is reading · they are eating
Use the present simple for routines. Use am, is or are with an ing verb for an action now.
We drink water every day. She is reading now.
boat
Likes and wishes
like reading · enjoys playing · want to swim
Use an ing form after enjoy. After want or wants, use to and a base verb.
She enjoys playing games. He wants to eat.
pickaxe
Past actions and ability
helped · watched · visited · went · could
Yesterday and last night refer to the past. Could shows ability in the past.
Yesterday, we went to the zoo. I could swim when I was five.
portal
Future plans
I am going to · she is going to · we are going to
Use am, is or are going to, then a base verb.
We are going to make sandwiches.
cat
Give a reason
Why? · because
Because tells us the reason for an action. Match the reason to the situation.
She wears a coat because it is cold.
castle
Compare towers
taller than · shorter than · bigger than
Compare the height or size of the two objects.
Tower B is taller than Tower A.

curriculum.document: KSSR (Semakan 2017) Standards-Based English Language Curriculum, Sekolah Kebangsaan, Year 4; Bahagian Pembangunan Kurikulum, Ministry of Education Malaysia, April 2018
curriculum.title: English Language Year 4 (SK) DSKP — Primary Year 4 Syllabus
curriculum.grammarPages: Printed syllabus pages 45–47 (PDF pages 59–61); earlier grammar in Appendix 1, printed pages 53–54 (PDF pages 67–68). Relevant learning standards: printed pages 26, 31 and 35–36 (PDF pages 40, 45 and 49–50).
learningStandards: 4.2.1: Language for giving reasons for simple opinions, supported here by because sentences.
4.2.3: Language for describing basic daily routines, supported here by guided sentence ordering.
4.2.4: Suitable language for describing people and objects, supported here by ownership and comparison statements.
4.3.1: Capital letters and sentence punctuation, practised here in guided word ordering; the full standard concerns writing at discourse level.
2.1.2: Language for describing past experiences; classroom speaking practice is needed to assess the full standard.
3.2.2: Reading for specific details is supported by short clues; the full standard expects simple texts of one or two paragraphs.
curriculum.note: Original 4B foundation practice: exactly 20 low and 20 lower-medium activities. Short direct prompts, mostly two-choice blocks and short word banks reduce reading load; the second level adds a small context or grammar choice. Selected Year 4 grammar includes quantity, possession, verb patterns, past actions and could, going to, because and comparisons; present simple and continuous are explicitly recycled in the Year 4 syllabus. Difficulty labels are teacher-facing design categories, not PBD or CEFR performance judgements.
